models.model: The present indicative plural and second-plural imperative are both hęriað. An assertion about the subject differs from a command to the addressees. The third-person wish uses hęrien.
hine ondrǣdendum
models.analysis: Accusative person feared within a nominalized dative plural participial phrase; grammar agent expressly corrected provisional him to hine.

models.model: ðā hyngrendan
models.analysis: Article with weak accusative masculine plural present participle naming hungry people.

models.model: Ondrǣdendum is dative plural because the people are beneficiaries. Hine is accusative because it is the object governed by fear within that phrase. The outer case and the inner verb's government remain separate.

The participle names people characterized by fearing or hunger and takes the case demanded by the noun phrase's role. It is nonfinite: present participle is not a person/tense statement, and these phrases have no finite verb.
